title: Artifacts Workflows
description: Apply Artifacts to real-world workflows — rapid prototyping, data visualization, interactive tools, and team collaboration.

data.text: The real value of Artifacts emerges when you integrate them into actual work workflows. This lesson walks through practical workflows where Artifacts save hours of work: rapid prototyping, data visualization, creating interactive documentation, and building shareable tools for teams.

Before committing engineering resources to a feature, use Artifacts to prototype the user experience. Describe the feature, Claude builds an interactive HTML prototype, and you test the UX before writing any production code. This is faster than sketching, more realistic than wireframes, and requires zero frontend skills.

data.title: Rapid prototyping prompt
data.content: Prompt: 'Create an HTML artifact for a dashboard that shows social media metrics. Include cards for followers, engagement rate, and top posts. Make it look like a modern SaaS dashboard with a sidebar. I want to show this to stakeholders before we build the real thing.'

data.text: Upload a CSV or describe your data, and ask Claude to create a visualization artifact. Claude can generate bar charts, line charts, pie charts, and interactive dashboards using JavaScript libraries. This is useful for quick analysis, presentations, and reports.

Instead of static documentation, create interactive artifacts that demonstrate concepts. An interactive anatomy diagram, a step-by-step calculator, or a configurator can make documentation far more engaging. Claude builds the interactivity; you focus on the content.

data.title: How to share and collaborate on artifacts:
items: Copy the artifact code and share it via GitHub, Google Drive, or any code host
Take a screenshot of the rendered artifact for quick sharing
Use the artifact as a starting point for a developer to implement in production
Export HTML artifacts as standalone files that anyone can open in a browser

data.title: Best practices for productive artifact workflows:
items: Name your conversations clearly so you can find artifacts later
Version your artifacts by creating new conversations for major changes
Document the prompt that produced a good artifact — reproducibility matters
Test artifacts on different screen sizes if they are web-based
Keep artifacts focused — one artifact, one purpose

data.title: Artifacts are not production-ready code
data.text: Artifacts are excellent for prototyping, demonstration, and learning. They are not designed to be production-ready code. Always have a developer review and refactor artifact code before using it in production systems.

items.question: Can I download an artifact?
items.answer: Yes. Code artifacts have a copy button, and HTML artifacts can be saved as files. You can also screenshot the rendered view.

items.question: Are artifacts private?
items.answer: Artifacts in your Claude conversations are private to your account, just like the rest of your chat history.

items.question: Can I edit an artifact after generation?
items.answer: Yes — ask Claude to make changes in the conversation, or copy the code and edit it in your own editor.

items.question: Do artifacts work in the free tier?
items.answer: Yes, Artifacts are available in both free and Pro tiers.

data.title: Artifact workflows summary
points: Use Artifacts for rapid prototyping before committing engineering resources
Create data visualizations by describing your data and desired chart type
Build interactive documentation that is more engaging than static text
Share artifacts by copying code or exporting as standalone files
Artifacts are prototypes, not production-ready code — always review before deployment
